Following the progress of the game, it only gets even BETTER!!!

Unfortunately, this isn't the game you're looking for. If you've ever played Starcraft 2 custom map Lottery Defense, the grind is comparable. Absolutely not worth more than $1, it really should be a free game on mini-clip or Kongregate the content is incredibly lacking but to clarify, more content wouldn't fix the sea of problems this game has. The weapons are all boring, you're locked into a projectile heavy build for the vast majority of the game, and even when you unlock others, the melee is almost utterly partial cleaves 25-50% that can only be aimed left or right so you always miss below you. The spells are all gimped, or boring and mediocre. Clearly someone likes projectile builds in this genre. The absolute only redeeming factor, is you can play a Vampire Survivors type of game with friends, but it is a horrible bastardization of the game, so really you'll just be mad at yourself for trying to get a friend to play this with you. Especially if it is the first time they've played this genre, you'll pretty much guarantee you'll never convince them to play another one. I could go on and on, and the positives end about 5 minutes into the game and after that it is all just bad versions of everything that have been done better in every game like this. The biggest red flag I should have noticed, is that apparently they just recently added Vacuum to the game to gather xp... how the hell was that an after-thought....? EDIT: I finished this review, wen't to return to my game to leave it and close the game when I realized that the most silly thing in the game is how often mini-bosses spawn, that you'll only be killing without running around if you're a projectile glass cannon build. (I'm playing a tank) This is my chat log as I'm about to close the game; A miniboss has spawned TIP: You can open Chests by hitting them or walking over them A miniboss has spawned You found 10 gold A miniboss has spawned Limit Break, your primary weapon does +100% damage A miniboss has spawned You found 9 gold A miniboss has spawned You found 6 gold A miniboss has spawned

Game got a good feel for a "survivors" but there is some issues that limit this game to have a positive review. First: Some important mechanics to progression are locked behind a 25 achievements grind fest. Second: As a survivors game, you got swarms of enemies but the dev ( read some of his past post about the topic) think its a good idea to limit the numbers of enemies you can hit with a weapon ( there is no issue with this in "vampire survivors" or other "survivors" game so...¯\_(ツ)_/¯ ) Third: Some mechanics are badly explained like the Guardians ( first one spawn after 30 min but the next one spawn like only 2-5 min after. Four: Difficulty is badly balanced, So you were able to escape the first map with no bonus to damage ( which are locked behind the said grind fest mentioned earlier, here is the second/third/+ map with enemies who have an increase in damage and health ( second map is 12.5% increase, third is 25 %, etc ) Edit: So went foward with the grind to see if the game get better with "new" mechanics. Answer is no, apart from the little boost its offer for the first few maps, still have to grind even more to unlock some of the basic merchants for pets and others features. Game feel like a huge time waster which give hope it get better later in the run when is it not, absolute garbage in the "survivors" genre.

Great ideas but poorly executed. First and foremost the attacks and player hitbox are terrible. You don't know where your hits will go and when you'll take a hit. Second the meta UI is unintuitive. Third the choice of making a melee character the 'first' character is terrible because it's extremely difficult to play with; the axe doesn't really hit enemies below you, yet the chest and exit are below you. The melee play style is not for beginners. This is a great expansion on the vampire survivors ideas but the execution and design leave much to be desired. I think another game designer and developer will take these ideas and polish them.

Refunded. While the core idea and depth tickle my senses, playing it was sadly a turnoff overall. It is very difficult playing solo, and the melee situation is just plain inacceptable for a game in 2024, no matter the low price. Apart from not knowing if a tree is blocking your way or not (you will eventually learn it I guess, because the maps never change), the hitboxes really blow and the attack area is a joke, like some other guy pointed out here. Objective (Map 1) is to go "south" or down, but your weapon doesn't hit in that direction. So you have to rely on either evasive maneuvers like Captain Kirk or on finding other weapons that might hit in that direction. But even with a mage and his dragon stick, it felt like a clunky mess. You get spammed with tutorial tipps, which is of course nice. But they are random, not situational. For real: when I'm trying to survive solo and am struggling with one of the annoying mechanics, the turned off lights, I'm not interested in learning about auras that are a thing in multiplayer! Overall I do recommend to try out the game. If you found it, it might be something for you. But keep an eye on the refund timer. There are cheaper and technically much better games out there. The difficulty seems to be balanced for multiplayers.

This game does a lot of interesting things, but does all of them badly. The developer actually doesn't seem to understand what makes a survivors game fun. -No player base to take advantage of multiplayer, even though an achievement is tied to it and it seems like some of the gameplay would be less "grindy" with it -Limiting targets on AOE weapons is one of the dumbest design decisions I've ever seen in a game, from any company -Incredibly grindy gameplay, and I'm someone who is great at these sorts of games. I have all the achievements in other, similar, titles such as Halls of Torment. And that game isn't easy either -Esoteric unlocks that take quite a bit of research. If this game had an actual player base, a lot of people would be lost -Ranged enemies that auto-hit are ridiculous. They make an already grindy game much harder, and you need to build around them. Not great -Hitboxes often have no correlation to the models you see. Ridiculous -Sometimes the game just breaks completely, you load up and you're the starting melee character, but you can't move or do anything -The developer personally reads, and ignores, all constructive criticism on their game. The discussion forum is full of good ideas, better ideas than their own, that they reject It's literally a title that should be free. Someone needs to make sure that a teenager didn't make this game.

Completely and totally unbalanced mess. I gave it more than a fair shot but it's just pissing me off with boneheaded design choices from bell to bell, primarily the inane decision to seemingly balance gameplay around you playing in multiplayer with no lowered scaling for solo players. Certainly feels that way anyway. [b]If you're here for multiplayer you can probably disregard this entire review.[/b] Weapons balancing is atrocious, some of the worst I've seen in the genre. Melee weapons have awful range and dead zones as well as limited hits before despawning. Magic weapons so far are mostly weak, the starting fire staff being the only viable option, and familiars have genuinely worthless range and damage. Ranged physical weapons in comparison are just ridiculously good, especially the Longbow, Kick and Javelin. Unfortunately each character starts with their own weapon, and most of them are terrible and you need to RNG while levelling for a good one. The sheer GRIND early is insanity. Unlocking any of the actually useful meta upgrades requires you to farm at least 25 achievements, which'll take you at least 7 or 8 hours being generous. During which time you will experience the exciting gameplay of standing in specific spots to farm experience because enemies ramp up so hard in numbers and power that moving around for unlocks is tantamount to suicide outside of specific timings. Of course, you won't be able to get so far because each new area beefs the enemies even more to the point where you require RNG meta progression to stand any chance by the third area. You heard me. There are marbles you can randomly get at a low chance, with random rarity, which you can slap onto weapons to power their base damage up by up to +30%. But guess what? The strongest ones are not only insanely rare (I've seen none so far) but have an 85% failure rate to apply! :D I might keep going back to it out of spite, but this game really makes me mad. It's got some interesting ideas, the basic gameplay is there, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the balancing is unforgivably bad for solo play, and the grind required to unlock any of the fun stuff is terrible. Perhaps in multiplayer mode most of these problems don't exist and you're free to try more varied builds with less stress, but I'm not here for that. -3-

Fantasy Survivors is a rather generically named, criminally under recognized, and super awesome Vampire Survivors type co-op game. There are a million VS clones out there at this point and I have played and enjoyed many. However, I specifically wanted to find one that focused on multiplayer co-op. And thus I made a leap of faith and tried Fantasy Survivors. And, oh boy, what a wise choice that was. How has this game flown so under the radar?! While it’s clearly based on the Vampire Survivor game sub-type (Bullet Hell/Heaven, Horde Survivor, or whatever the genre will eventually settle in on), it has some standout features. --True co-op (not local only nor having player 2 be the boring echo player --Map design that rewards a bit of player exploration and planning --Almost class like character design where certain combinations work best on certain heroes --Build sorting where you can essentially customize your pool without banning or re-rolls --Less of an RNG casino feel and more of a traditional game load-out puzzle --RPG like progression where the player is doing usual VS meta, but also assigning crafting-like buffs to weapons. The gear, marbles, and component drops progression overshadows the usual meta stuff. --Not just solo or duo, and it works best with several players I only have two negatives to offer. Fantasy Survivors doesn’t support cloud saves so bouncing between PC and Steam Deck is a chore and that is a place these type of games shine. A real shame on that one. It also has rather iffy controller support. The second point is more of a side effect of the game being real time including level ups (for multiplayer reasons) and said level ups having several RPG like mouse options (improve damage, or range, or maximum targets for item 1 or…). Character movement is ASDW. Not ideal, but I am over the controller disappointment. Mostly. Anyways, I have had a grand time unlocking and grinding stuff while playing with a buddy in this VS type game. It has been a rather fresh experience as usually these games are usually an almost idle/ second screen type game that I grind out meta solo. I highly recommend anyone curious take a peek. It’s well worth the 7 or so bucks.

This game is AWESOME - finally a solid Co-Op horde survivors game! Great meta progression/unlock system. Strong, strong recommend. (Not totally brainless, early game you could get carried a bit by randos in a public game just for a little boost! Getting a build in this game is super important - I'll say no more though!)

almost 40 hours into the game, haven't even hit survivor level 3. This game has been released for over a year and the balance is still very broken. This is probably one of my hardest reviews to write because I really wanted to like this game. They have recently re balanced early game progression supposedly, but after sinking this many hours into the game and only seeing Maybe 20-25% of the content im done. The fact that no one on the team took the time to start over fresh save files solo to see how atrocious early game is tells me all I need to know. Maybe I will try their next game after they learn a little more about game design. As it stand now though, it's a hard No. There are way too many games out there that do this genre better, often times for a lower price point.

I have to unfortunately give this game a thumbs down, even though I really want to like it. On the surface it's a multiplayer focused Vampire Survivors game with a ton of characters and meta-progression. However in playing it is just full of unfun design decisions. The game prioritizes "Survivor Levels" as the gameplay mechanic locks. But you need 25 achievements to unlock the first set of additional mechanics. Which can take anywhere from 7 to 10 hours. During that time you'll start to realize there are only really about 5 weapons, and every other weapon is a clone of the original but with a different model. Then the other realizations start happening. Enemy hitboxes are much larger than you'd expect. Your weapon hitboxes are smaller than you'd expect, even after leveling them up. Meta upgrades are more expensive then they really need to be and characters really have fewer differences then you want. There are also just noticeable programming bugs you'd expect to have been ironed out very early on. Like weapons that have a few frames at their starting length before "jumping" to their new upgraded range. And the obscure way "learning a weapon" knowledge is actually obtained. Overall the entire game is just disappointing. It promises a lot of good things but it never delivers. If you're looking for a game to play with your friends and you really set your expectations low maybe you will enjoy this game. But honestly it's just a case study of how a few short-sighted decisions can truly effect the quality of what could have been an otherwise great game.

Fantasy Survivors, a survivor-like that gives you nothing you'd generally expect from a game in it's genre. PROs: - It's multiplayer - It's cheap. - Once you have enough gear, you can set a loadout, to reduce the amount of garbage items you'll get offered. - The dev is still working on it, I guess? CONs: - There's no lobby system, 1 friend has to start a run and then wait for the rest to join. - It's only balanced around multiplayer, the singleplayer experience is horrendous. - You can't get some wild level of attack speed and turn into a blender. - You can't make your projectiles or abilities multiple times the size of your character. - All aoe weapons have a target cap(?). - Even the swords have a target cap, with a horrific attack animation that struggles with any form of y axis movement. - I can't say for certain about all characters, but every character I (and my friends) have unlocked so far has been through pure rng, you have to just run a level enough and hope you get gear/characters instead of just gold. - The entire Marble system. - The Survivor Level system. All in all, it's an aggressively mid game that's only true redeeming quality is that you can play it with your friends and laugh at the absurdity that is realising the quality of the game you're playing. Kinda fun with friends/10.

This is the most poorly balanced game I've ever played. The first level is so easy you can literally afk it. Then as you progress through the levels, the dev's idea of a challenge is to make every level a labyrinth. The game has no map or mini map to guide you. You have to spend hours attempting each map over and over again to memorize the sprawling paths. Then they decide to kick the difficulty up a notch by making ranged enemies auto-hit you with undodgeable attacks that kill you in two hits. By the way, these ranged enemies spawn 50 at a time so you just instantly die. 90% of the items and characters in this game are useless. The meta progression takes so long that I'm 50 hours in and I'd estimate I'm about 5% of the way through the gold upgrades. The only good thing this game has going for it is co-op, but there's no lobby feature so you have to start a run, then invite everyone, then everyone joins the run late and everyone wasted precious time since each map is severely time limited before guardians spawn and kill you in one hit. They also made monsters spawn in a circle around each player, so if you're not standing right on top of your friends then you make monsters spawn on them and kill your team instantly.

I have been addicted to this game for the last week or so and I love it. There is a good sense of progression as you make your way through the survivor levels. Starting out you feel quite weak and just completing the map is difficult solo. Once you unlock more weapons and characters you can take on harder maps and difficulties. The game will not just give you some of the strongest gear in the game as you must farm materials to craft them, which makes it feel like you have earned the power spike once you can finally craft them. I hope more players try out the game because it is even more fun co-op. It's not perfect though, trying to find out how to unlock certain items and how to unlock more maps can be confusing. I find myself searching through the discord server to find most of this info from previous questions people have asked. Though it you like to play a game that doesn't just spoon feed you all the information like most games this could be a plus for you. Overall, Great game and price! I recommend

I'm almost 20 hours in at the time of posting this and I feel like I'm just scratching the surface of this game. It deserves way more attention than it has gotten.

Overall I do enjoy the game but I do have some feedback for things that I think would be a source of improvement 1) better infrastructure for joining a friends private game, the join on through steam is less than ideal and the ability to make a sort of group waiting room would be nice 2) the maps are a bit quiet, having theme music would be a lot more enjoyable, given that the ads for the game have rock music playing over the matches. 3) the games unlock loop can be a bit of a grind, to the point that I am actually a bit worried that once I get everything unlocked I might end up not wanting to play more because of a feeling of fatigue with it. All of that said I do enjoy the game and enjoy the character unlocks and the item options and builds. I do have issues with a few maps but overall I do enjoy playing it and love being able to play with friends. There is also something nice where higher tier players have hopped into open runs I have had and helped me make it to the end, making me want to do the same for newer players and help them out.
